This is a list of events and standings for the [[Professional Fighters League]], a mixed martial arts organization based in the United States, for the 2024 season.

== Background ==
In January 2024, PFL announced that it would discontinue it's Women's Featherweight division – which had existed in the tournament format since 2018 season – and replace it with the Women's Flyweight division.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2024/01/pfl-2024-divisions-womens-flyweight-featherweight|title=PFL scraps women's featherweight division, replaces it with women's flyweight|date=January 24, 2024|work=[[MMAjunkie.com]]|author=Nolan King}}</ref> Following to PFL's acquisition of [[Bellator MMA]] in late 2023, some of the Bellator fighters are scheduled to take part in the 2024 tournaments.<ref name=mmaf24>{{cite web|url=https://www.mmafighting.com/2024/2/20/24078153/pfl-fighters-dates-2024-regular-season-las-vegas-card-ufc-300|title=PFL announces first fighters, dates for 2024 regular season, including Las Vegas card the night before UFC 300|date=February 20, 2024|publisher=mmafighting.com|author=Guilherme Cruz}}</ref>

== Format ==
The PFL points system is based on results of the match.  The winner of a fight receives 3 points.  If the fight ends in a draw, both fighters will receive 1 point. A no-contest will be scored as a draw.  The bonus for winning a fight in the first, second, or third round is 3 points, 2 points, and 1 point respectively. The bonus for winning in the third round requires a fight be stopped before 4:59 of the third round.  No bonus point will be awarded if a fighter wins via decision. If a fighter misses weight, the opponent (should they comply with weight limits) will receive 3 points due to a walkover victory, regardless of winning or losing the bout, with the fighter who missed weight being deducted 1 point;  if the non-offending fighter subsequently wins with a stoppage, all bonus points will be awarded. A fighter who was unable to compete for any reason, will receive a 1-point
penalty (-1 point in the standings). The fighters who made weight will not receive a walkover, but will earn points and contracted purse amounts based on their performance in the altered matchup.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2021 Official Rules|url=https://pflmma-prod.s3.amazonaws.com/assets/downloads/2021_Rules_and_Regulations_4-26-2021.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210507024409/https://pflmma-prod.s3.amazonaws.com/assets/downloads/2021_Rules_and_Regulations_4-26-2021.pdf |archive-date=2021-05-07 }}</ref>

== PFL Europe ==
Starting in 2024, PFL Europe featured European MMA fighters. The format followed the same as other PFL Seasons, with the winner receiving a $100,000 prize.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PFL and DAZN announce historic media rights partnership for Europe |url=https://www.pflmma.com/news/pfl-and-dazn-announce-historic-media-rights-partnership-for-europe |website=Professional Fighters League}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=PROFESSIONAL FIGHTERS LEAGUE BOLSTERS GLOBAL EXECUTIVE TEAM WITH JULIA BOYADJIEVA JOINING AS VP OF INTERNATIONAL EVENT OPERATIONS AND GM OF PFL EUROPE |url=https://www.pflmma.com/news/professional-fighters-league-bolsters-global-executive-team-with-julia-boyadjieva-joining-as-vp-of-international-event-operations-and-gm-of-pfl-europe |website=Professional Fighters League}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=PFL CONTINUES GLOBAL EXPANSION WITH LAUNCH OF PFL EUROPE |url=https://mmauk.net/2022/07/14/pfl-continues-global-expansion-with-launch-of-pfl-europe/ |website=MMA UK}}</ref>
